summary: The gate is wired, scoped and non-vacuous on a MISSING file, and the five test cases the script's header names all exist (GracefulReleaseMeterTest x4, FaultInjectingStoreTest x1), so the presence/position/total division is honestly labelled. But the predicate itself does not hold on its own subject: the eight-line window starts at the @Override and reaches PAST the end of a short verb into the NEXT method's record(...), so half the real store's verbs pass with their meter call deleted. Measured by deleting each of the twelve record("<verb>") lines from a copy of sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/FaultInjectingStore.java and running the gate on each: getRange, put, multipart, delete and capabilities all exit 0 -- the gate reports '12 verb(s) metered' over a file that meters eleven. capabilities is one of the three verbs M5.29's history names, and it is the one this gate is supposed to have caught. The fixture set cannot see this because in unmetered.java the unmetered verb (presign) is the LAST member in the file, so nothing follows it to lend it a record(. Two further holes measured: a target with zero @Override exits 0 printing '0 verb(s) metered' -- the same examined-nothing pass the row says is closed, closed only for the missing-file case -- and 'first statement' is not what is checked, so a record(...) on one branch four lines down, or a record( inside a comment, both pass. No production code and no object-store request path is touched, so nothing here moves a request rate. Three findings block; the printf word-splitting in the failure output is minor.

findings.title: the eight-line window reaches into the NEXT method, so five of the real store's twelve verbs pass with record(...) deleted
findings.failure_scenario: window = '\n'.join(src[i:i + 8]) starts at the @Override and is a fixed line count, not a body extent, so for any verb shorter than eight lines the window includes the following @Override and its record(...). Measured on this tree: copy sequencer/src/test/java/binjava/sequencer/FaultInjectingStore.java, delete one record("<verb>") line, run ./scripts/check-fault-store-records.sh <copy>. getRange (:596), put (:602), multipart (:659), delete (:676) and capabilities (:682) each exit 0 with 'ok 12 verb(s) metered' -- the count is still read from grep -c '@Override' so the success line asserts twelve meters over eleven. capabilities is one of the three verbs M5.29's history names as having shipped unmetered, and it is the one an implementer would expect this gate to have caught. Of those five, only capabilities has any per-verb assertion in the suite (calls("capabilities")); getRange, put, multipart and delete have neither a gate nor a case, so the exact defect the row exists to stop -- a verb whose record call is absent, invisible until a release-path floor reds with no defect present -- ships green today for four verbs. The comment on line 65 asserts the opposite ('a long one would swallow the next method'), which is true of the window that was chosen, not only of a longer one. The fixture set cannot observe this: buildSrc/src/test/resources/fault-store-fixtures/unmetered.java:16 puts presign last in the class, so no later record( exists to lend it one; move presign above get in that fixture and the harness case refusesAVerbThatIsNotMetered goes green on exit 0 while asserting exit 1. A body-extent predicate (brace depth from the signature's opening brace, or 'up to the next @Override / next member') is what the claim needs.

findings.title: a target with zero @Override passes with 'ok 0 verb(s) metered' -- the examined-nothing pass the row claims is closed
findings.failure_scenario: The existence check at :49 closes only the missing-file case. A file that exists but contains no @Override produces MISSING='' and falls through to ok "$COUNT verb(s) metered" with COUNT=0, exit 0. Measured: a two-line class with no members exits 0 printing '0 verb(s) metered'. This is not hypothetical -- FaultInjectingStore.java is exactly 700 lines, i.e. sitting on check-file-size.sh's ceiling, so the next change to it is a split, and a split that leaves the verbs in a new sibling file and the fields in the guarded one leaves this gate green forever over zero verbs. Same outcome if someone converts the verbs to a composed or absent annotation (@Override is optional in Java). The harness case theRealFaultInjectingStoreIsFullyMetered asserts out contains 'verb(s) metered', which '0 verb(s) metered' satisfies, so the suite would not notice either. A floor on COUNT -- fail if it is 0, or better, pin the expected verb count against the SPI's method list -- is what makes the success line mean something.

findings.title: 'as its first statement' is asserted in three places and is not what the script checks; a one-branch record and a commented-out one both pass
findings.failure_scenario: The failure message at :78 tells the author 'Every @Override must call record("<verb>") as its first statement', the pre-commit hook name and AGENTS.md's row say the verb is 'metered', and the backlog done-cell says the nine-line far-away fixture is refused 'because a verb metering on only one branch is the defect one step subtler than the one this gate is named for'. The predicate is substring 'record(' anywhere in eight lines, which is neither first-statement nor all-branches. Measured: a verb with 'if (k == null) { return "unmetered-path"; }' above record("get") -- metering exactly one branch, four lines down -- exits 0; a verb whose only occurrence is '// TODO: record("get") once the meter lands' exits 0. far-away.java is refused by DISTANCE, not by position, so it pins nothing about branches; rewrite it with the same two early throws two lines shorter and it passes. Concrete failure: the next person adding a verb to FaultInjectingStore reads :78, believes position is enforced, and writes record(...) below refuseIfPartitioned -- which is precisely the placement GracefulReleaseMeterTest's four named cases exist to forbid, and which the gate's own header at :20-31 says the gate cannot see. Either check the first non-comment statement of the body (the claim as written), or state the predicate as presence-anywhere-in-the-body and drop the first-statement wording from the message, the fixture javadoc and the backlog cell.

findings.title: the failure output word-splits the offending signature into one word per line
findings.failure_scenario:
printf '           %s
' $(echo "$MISSING" | ...) leaves the command substitution unquoted, so bash splits on IFS and printf cycles the format per word. Measured on the shipped fixture: the single line 'buildSrc/.../unmetered.java:16  @Override public String presign(String k, long ttl) {' prints as nine lines -- 'presign(String', 'k,', 'long', 'ttl)', '{'. The sed fallback after || never runs because printf does not fail, and the tr/sed pipeline round-trips 
 to \v and back for no effect. The gate still exits 1, so this is cosmetic, but it is the only output an author sees at the moment the gate refuses, and the harness case asserts only contains("not metered"), so no test constrains it. printf '%s
' "$MISSING" | sed 's/^/           /' is the whole of it.
